newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's cleanup measures after Tokyo Bay spill.
newsitem.headline: Japan's cleanup measures after Tokyo Bay spill.

text.p: Following is a list of measures being taken to clean up a oil spill from the supertanker Diamond Grace, which leaked an estimated 1,550 kilolitres (kl) of crude after scraping a reef in Tokyo Bay on Wednesday:

Oil recovery ships -- About a dozen are in operation in Tokyo Bay. The Seiryumaru, the largest, can recover about 1,000 kl of oil mixed in with seawater. The other vessels are designed for coastal operations, which means they cannot operate in heavy seas.

Vacuum Oil Collectors -- A series of large floating devices connected to a mother ship by tubes. Pumps on the mother ship suck oil and seawater through the openings of the oil collectors. They are capable of collecting 50 kl of the mixture per hour. The apparatus costs more than 10 million yen ($87,700) per unit and is said to perform poorly in adverse weather.
Surface active agents -- Similar to household detergent, only less toxic. The agents turn oil resins into small particles to help them decompose.

Oil absorption sheets -- Thin sheets of cloth made of synthetic fibre. The sheets are thrown on to the oil spill and recovered having absorbed spillage. A package of 100 pieces of two-feet-by-two-feet sheet costs about 100,000 yen ($877). Good for all types of weather.
(Source: The Petroleum Association of Japan) ($1=114 yen)
